title: Leveraging serum CHI3L1 and machine learning for non-invasive liver fibrosis diagnostics
abstract: This study was aimed to develop non-invasive liver fibrosis diagnostic model using chitinase 3-like protein 1 (CHI3L1) based on machine learning (ML).1,011 follow-up patients (556 training/455 validation) were enrolled, staging fibrosis via transient elastography (F01, F2, F23, F34, and F4). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters were collected. Fibrosis-related indicators were selected by differential analysis and correlation analysis. ML models were developed, optimized, and validated. Of 23 initial laboratory indicators, 15 indicators were selected to developed a 5-stage liver fibrosis diagnostic model (XG-Boost, FIB5-15, area under the curve [AUC] = 0.93, sensitivity=0.70, specificity=0.93). This was refined to a 7-indicator model (FIB5-7, area under the ROC curve [AUC] = 0.98). By merging F2/F23 and F34/F4, a 3-category optimized model (FIB3-7, AUC=0.94) and a 2-category model (FIB2-7, AUC=0.95) were created to identify reversible fibrosis. The final FIB2-7 model significantly outperformed aspartate aminotransferase‑to‑platelet ratio index (APRI) and FIB-4 ( p < 0.001). The CHI3L1-related liver fibrosis models are applicable across multiple clinical scenarios.

title: Circular-economy residual-value assessment of retired lithium-ion batteries via degradation prediction and game-theoretic subsidies
abstract: Large-scale retirement of lithium-ion batteries enables second-life use in decentralized energy communities, yet capacity-degradation prediction, residual-value assessment, and subsidy allocation are treated in isolation. This study proposes an integrated circular-economy framework linking battery-state prediction with community-level incentive coordination. A physics-constrained transfer-learning hybrid model estimates capacity trajectories and remaining useful life, achieving a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.97%, R 2 of 0.960, and cross-chemistry transfer RMSE of 1.05%. A dynamic residual-value mapping function and operational degradation-burden index characterize health losses. A Stackelberg leader-follower game is formulated and transformed into single-level optimization via KKT (Karush-Kuhn-Tucker) reformulation, with a dynamic subsidy-allocation mechanism redistributing equilibrium subsidies by degradation contribution, participation duration, and circular-economy factors. Experiments on 240 battery aging samples and a 60-prosumer community show the proposed mechanism yields welfare of 3,610 CNY/day, outperforming fixed uniform allocation under varying subsidy intensities and perturbations.

title: Rational construction of interfacial photocatalysts toward outstanding performance in energy and evironmental applications
abstract: Interfacial photocatalysts with precisely engineered junctions are critical for overcoming the performance limitations of conventional photocatalytic systems, as they enable efficient charge transfer, suppress carrier recombination, and enhance surface redox kinetics. This review first outlines the rational design principles for interfacial photocatalysts and precise interfacial control, highlighting advanced engineering strategies—including asymmetric single-atom doping, construction of a step-scheme built-in electric field, and spatial decoupling of dual cocatalysts. We then decipher the underlying physicochemical mechanisms using operando characterizations and theoretical simulations, transforming the traditional "black-box" catalysis into a visualized six-step cascade of charge transfer and molecular activation. The transformative utility of these interfaces is demonstrated in high-efficiency energy conversion and environmental remediation, with a particular focus on the paradigm shift from passive mineralization of emerging contaminants to proactive "Waste-to-Wealth" upcycling of plastics and biomass. Finally, we discuss challenges and future directions in reactor scale-up, durability, and AI-driven materials discovery.

title: Characterizing cellular receptor dynamics in live fluorescence imaging using stochastic modeling and machine learning
abstract: Abstract Particle dynamics determine the orchestration of molecular signaling in cellular processes. A wide range of subdiffusive motions has been described at the cell interior and membrane, corresponding to different environmental constraints. However, the standard methods for motion analysis, embedded in a diffusion-based framework, lack robustness for capturing the complexity of stochastic dynamics. This work develops a classification method to detect the five main stochastic laws modeling particle dynamics accurately. The method builds on machine-learning techniques that use features properly designed to capture the intrinsic geometric properties of trajectories governed by the different processes. This guarantees the accurate classification of observed dynamics in an interpretable and explainable framework. The main asset of this approach is its capability to distinguish different subdiffusive behaviors making it a privileged tool for biological investigations. The robustness to localization error and motion composition is proven, ensuring its reliability on experimental data. Moreover, the classification of composed trajectories is investigated, showing that the method can uncover the path’s mono-vs bi-dynamics nature. The method is used to study the dynamics of membrane receptors CCR5, involved in HIV infection. Comparing the basal state to an agonist-bound state which displays potent anti-HIV-1 activity, we show that the latter affects the natural dynamic state of receptors, thus clarifying the link between movement and receptor activation.

title: Interpretable multimodal MRI fusion in Alzheimer’s disease classification using extended parallel multilink joint ICA and 3D ResNet
abstract: Accurate identification of Alzheimer's disease (AD) stages is important for improving clinical understanding and supporting early-stage assessment. In this study, two multimodal MRI fusion strategies were developed to integrate structural MRI, resting-state functional MRI, and diffusion tensor imaging for pairwise binary classification among four groups: normal cognition (NC), subjective cognitive decline (SCD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD dementia (ADD). The extended parallel multilink joint independent component analysis (Epml-jICA) combined with a support vector machine (SVM) approach (machine learning) and the ensemble 3D ResNet model (deep learning) were evaluated on 664 participants with multimodal MRI. The results demonstrated that the optimal area under the receiver operating curve (AUROC) values for ADD vs. NC and SCD vs. NC were 95.68% and 81.25%, respectively. Furthermore, systematic interpretability analyses using SHAP, Grad-CAM, and anatomical localization of cross-modal important components were conducted, identifying model-associated imaging patterns that were consistent with prior AD-related findings and may provide insights into different disease stages.

title: Too rigid to strike: Excess desmin at Z-discs underlies a restrictive cardiomyopathy in GAN mice
abstract: Restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) is characterized by myocardial stiffness and impaired diastolic filling. While human giant axonal neuropathy (GAN) is linked to RCM with desmin accumulation, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We combined 3D tissue staining, electron microscopy, and echocardiography to investigate RCM phenotypes in GAN mice. Phenotypic profiling revealed atrial enlargement and impaired diastolic relaxation. Ultrastructural analysis demonstrated shortened I-bands and widened, hyper-dense Z-discs, correlating with elevated desmin density at Z-discs. To elucidate the biophysical principles driving this pathology, we developed an AI-guided multiscale computational model simulating the progression from molecular overcrowding to macro-level organ dysfunction. The modeling indicates that excess desmin crowding promotes aberrant inter-filament contacts, reduces linker-12 compliance, limits Z-disc elastic recoil, and physically restricts diastolic I-band re-extension. Collectively, our multidisciplinary findings establish an experiment-constrained mechanical framework linking desmin proteostasis failure to restrictive sarcomere dysfunction.

title: From pixels to conservation: Deep learning for automated monitoring of rare and endangered wildlife
abstract: Conservation of rare and endangered species requires scalable monitoring solutions to address accelerating biodiversity loss. Deep learning has transformed wildlife monitoring, enabling automated species identification, individual tracking, demographic inference, and behavioral analysis from camera traps, drones, and video surveillance. This review systematically analyzes 159 wildlife monitoring studies (2014-2026) across four technical domains: species recognition, individual re-identification, soft biometrics (age/sex estimation), and behavior/pose analysis. We examine architectural evolution across three architectural paradigms-CNN-based models, Attention & Sequence Architectures, and Foundation Models- documenting performance advances and ecological applications. Key challenges-environmental interference, data scarcity, domain shift, computational constraints-and optimization strategies, including data augmentation, transfer learning, and model compression, are systematically addressed. Case studies demonstrate real-world impact across diverse taxa: giant pandas, Amur tigers, great apes, and marine mammals. We identify critical research gaps and emerging opportunities in foundation model adaptation, multimodal learning, spatiotemporal modeling, and edge deployment. This review bridges computer vision research and conservation practice, providing actionable insights for developing robust, deployable monitoring systems that translate algorithmic advances into conservation impact.

title: Physics-informed self-supervised denoising for fluorescence microscopy via structure and intensity priors
abstract: Fluorescence microscopy images contain smooth, low-intensity backgrounds dominated by random noise and brighter biological signals with complex textures. We incorporate these structural and intensity characteristics into self-supervised denoising through two complementary modules. Structure-adaptive probabilistic masking (SAPM) uses local variance to reduce masking in textured regions while increasing masking in redundant backgrounds. Intensity-aware weighted loss (IA-Loss) reweights optimization according to local brightness to improve preservation of high-intensity signals under signal-dependent noise. Using Noise2Void (N2V) as the baseline, we developed structure- and intensity-prior-guided Noise2Void (SI-N2V) with a Mamba-UNet backbone for global contextual modeling. Experiments on an in-house pathological dataset and public fluorescence microscopy datasets show that SAPM and IA-Loss independently improve denoising and achieve the largest gains when combined. IA-Loss also consistently improves several self-supervised denoising frameworks, supporting its use as a plug-and-play optimization module.

title: AI-assisted metabolomic profiling identifies candidate metabolites associated with diabetic kidney disease staging in a Korean cohort
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is commonly staged using albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), yet complementary molecular markers are needed. We profiled urine and serum metabolites from 92 Korean participants (72 with type 2 diabetes and 20 healthy controls) using gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (GC-MS/MS) and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). An exploratory restricted Boltzmann machine framework compared five DKD staging criteria and prioritized candidate metabolites; robustness was assessed against LASSO, linear support vector machine (SVM), and random forest using nested cross-validation. ACR-based staging showed the highest metabolomic discrimination. Urinary adenosine and 5′-methylthioadenosine decreased, whereas serum N2,N2-dimethylguanosine and cis -aconitic acid increased across ACR stages. Integration with a public renal tubular microarray dataset suggested NT5E as a cross-study network hub. These cross-sectional findings define candidate metabolite signatures associated with DKD severity and require external longitudinal validation before clinical translation.

title: Isolating error-based and reward-based learning in a real-world task via gradual perturbations in embodied VR
abstract: Error-based and reward-based mechanisms co-occur during real-world motor learning. In motor neuroscience, these two learning mechanisms are often studied in isolation via feedback manipulations in reductionistic laboratory tasks, such as point-to-point reaching movements. We previously demonstrated that in real-world tasks (playing pool billiards), a correction for a large error feedback can be rewarding enough to engage the reward learning mechanism, even in the absence of a reward signal (e.g. ball pocketing). Here, we examine whether these two learning mechanisms could be isolated via sensory feedback manipulations in a gradual perturbation task, while the perturbation-induced errors are smaller. Using mobile brain imaging (EEG) and Embodied Virtual Reality of pool billiards, where visual feedback is at the start veridical with the physical billiard setup, we introduce a gradual visual perturbation of the ball trajectories while keeping the real-world haptics and proprioception unchanged. N=32 participants underwent two sessions, learning gradual visuomotor rotation with either error or reward feedback. Behavioural and neural (Post Movement Beta Rebound over the Motor Cortex) markers recorded throughout the learning process showed a clear within-participant separation between the ways they learned the perturbation in the different sessions with the error and the reward feedback. Our results show how error- and reward-based learning mechanisms could be separated in a real-world task. Our framework and results open the way to AI-controlled manipulation of learning mechanisms to accelerate skill learning in medical (e.g. neurorehabilitation) and vocational uses (surgeons, sports).

title: Explainable AI molecularly imprinted polymer electrochemiluminescence biosensor for discriminative methamphetamine and amphetamine detection
abstract: Independent forensic quantification of methamphetamine (MA) and amphetamine (AMP) remains challenging due to their near-identical structures and overlapping electrochemical signatures. We report an end-to-end AI-integrated MIP-ECL biosensing framework employing target-specific MIP-NP/MWCNT/Nafion/Ir(pq) 2 (acac)/SPCE platforms. The Ir(III) luminophore within an MWCNT/Nafion matrix produced markedly superior ECL emission over the [Ru(bpy) 3 ] 2+ benchmark (40 mM DBAE, pH 8.0). MIP nanoparticles conferred high selectivity against structurally related interferents, validated in saliva, urine, and blood plasma, achieving detection limits of 0.11 ng mL −1 for MA and 0.28 ng mL −1 for AMP. A structured explainable machine learning pipeline employing CatBoost with Group-K-Fold cross-validation eliminated data leakage and achieved test R 2 values of 0.9864 (MA) and 0.9675 (AMP). SHAP analysis confirmed that model predictions were consistent with known electrochemical kinetics. This modular framework establishes a generalizable paradigm for intelligent MIP-ECL biosensing with direct applicability in forensic toxicology and point-of-care diagnostics.

title: Recurrent power outages and the mental health burden of grid reliability in Maryland
abstract: Abstract Power outages are becoming more frequent in the United States, yet their mental health consequences remain under-identified in clinical data. Maryland is a particularly relevant setting given its mental health service utilization rate of 42.2 per 1,000 population—nearly twice the national average—and its aging grid infrastructure under increasing climate stress. We combine high-frequency power outage records (15-minute intervals) with administrative inpatient claims from the Maryland Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project State Inpatient Database to estimate how outages affect mental-health-related hospitalizations from 2018 to 2023. In the baseline, we define severe outage exposure as the count of episodes exceeding the 75 th percentile of outage intensity and lasting at least one hour. Higher outage exposure is consistently associated with increased mental health hospitalization rates (IRR (Incidence Rate Ratio) ≈ 1.017, approximately a 1.7% increase). This association is robust to alternative severeity cutoffs (50 th and 90 th percentile), with effects concentrated in moderate-duration disruptions (1-3 hours) rather than prolonged outages. Instrumental-variable models using three grid infrastructure measures—transformer density, substation density, and transmission line density—indicate larger causal effects (IRR ≈ 1.35–1.52) than conventional fixed-effects models. Heterogeneity shows that effects are concentrated in large metropolitan areas and lower-poverty areas. Because hospitalization-based measures reflect both underlying need and access to care, these estimates likely understate the true population burden, particularly in underserved communities. These findings position grid reliability as a public health concern and highlight the importance of reducing recurrent short-duration outages, strengthening continuity of mental health care and medication access, and integrating health considerations into reliability planning for outage-prone communities.

title: Systematic image perturbations reveal persistent gaps between human and machine vision
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are promising computational models for understanding visual object recognition. Yet, whether DNNs use similar visual cues for object recognition as humans do remains unknown. We created an image set that systematically untangles global shape, internal parts, and texture information, and compared human recognition behavior against >200 DNNs spanning diverse architectures, training diets, and training objectives. No DNNs replicated humans' cue-reliance profile, including those with recurrence or specialized training. Fine-tuned text-image contrastive-trained models, regardless of architecture, were most human-like overall, but lost their human-alignment when the global shape was disrupted. Strikingly, all DNNs substantially underperformed humans when the global shape cue alone was critical to object recognition. Furthermore, alignment with ventral stream neural recordings in an existing database did not predict alignment to human behavior, and model performance does not always predict its human-alignment. Together, these findings reveal systematic and persistent differences between human and machine vision.

title: A systematic transcriptomic atlas and predictive framework for metabolite-driven T cell state transitions
abstract: Gut microbial and endogenous metabolites are key regulators at the interface of host metabolism and immunity, yet their global effects on human T cell states remain poorly defined. Here, we profile primary human T cell responses to 364 endogenous and microbiota-derived metabolites using high-throughput digital RNA with perturbation of genes sequencing (DRUG-seq), revealing structured transcriptional trajectories spanning baseline, metabolically primed, and highly activated states. We develop DRUG-seq-PerturbFormer, a multi-task deep learning framework that quantitatively captures perturbation magnitude and directionality across these states. This analysis identifies a subset of metabolites that robustly reprogram T cell transcriptional programs. In a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis model, representative candidates attenuated disease severity and were associated with suppression of inflammatory programs and partial restoration of immune homeostasis. Collectively, these findings show that metabolites act as signals shaping T cell function via transcription, nominating immunomodulatory targets for inflammatory diseases.

title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from multiple pretrained protein language models, aligns graph-based structural features with pretrained semantic embeddings for drugs under subspace constraints, and progressively refines drug-protein interaction representations through cascaded cross-modal signal propagation. Experiments on six benchmark datasets under standard, cold-start, and cross-domain settings demonstrate that SF-DTI achieves competitive performance relative to seven state-of-the-art baselines across evaluation scenarios. These results suggest that SF-DTI is a promising framework for DTI prediction and may support virtual screening, drug repositioning, and drug discovery.

title: Longitudinal pre-diagnostic blood samples predict osteoporosis risk
abstract: Cross-sectional biomarker discovery studies for degenerative diseases are limited by selection bias, post-diagnostic confounding, and high biological variability. Repeated pre-diagnostic sampling can address these limitations. We analyzed 538 plasma metabolomic profiles (1-6 samples per participant, yearly intervals) from 99 pre-diagnostic osteoporosis cases and 99 matched controls in the Danish Blood Donor Study. We compared performance of cross-sectional and longitudinal modeling using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression and random forest. Longitudinal LASSO modeling of metabolite trajectories achieved area under the curve (AUC) values between 0.67 and 0.76, outperforming cross-sectional models with AUC values of 0.57-0.63. Batch- and participant-independent validation of the best model demonstrated stable methodology (AUC: 0.70). The longitudinal data revealed that hippuric acid decreased over time in cases while increasing in controls. We conclude that longitudinal sampling costs more per participant, but the substantial information gain makes it a viable strategy when patient recruitment, not sampling capacity, is the bottleneck.

title: Real-time intelligence framework for microplastic monitoring and coastal resilience
abstract: The growing threat of microplastic contamination of the marine biosphere requires that monitoring technologies surpass the limitations of conventional approaches. This paper presents the development and validation of an integrated, machine learning-based framework for real-time detection and management of microplastics in coastal environments, whose primary contributions are real-time IoT-edge-cloud integration, multi-sensor fusion, and 72 h predictive modeling. We deployed a multi-sensor platform integrating hyperspectral imaging (400–2,500 nm) with IoT sensor networks at five monitoring locations over 18 months. The analytical pipeline employs a stacked ensemble of CNN, SVM, and random forest algorithms with soft-vote fusion. The framework achieved 96.3% accuracy in classifying microplastic polymers and successfully detected particles as small as 75 μm in diameter. The system demonstrated a strong correlation ( r = 0.92, p < 0.001) between predicted and observed pollution levels, enabling 72 h forecasting of pollution events with 84% probability. The framework processes samples 340% faster than traditional laboratory analysis while reducing operational costs by 67%. Through continuous real-time evaluation, this scalable solution will provide a quick instrument in a global network of coastal monitoring tools to create evidence-based policy and focused intervention approaches.

title: Dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding for anticancer peptide prediction via transfer learning
abstract: Computational identification of anti-tumor peptides (ACPs) is challenged by limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences. Standard transformer positional encodings fail to capture the periodicities and local motifs that govern peptide function. We propose dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), which replaces fixed sinusoidal encodings with parallel adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches, fused by a context-aware gating mechanism. A dual-stage transfer learning strategy pre-trains on 5,785 curated peptide sequences before fine-tuning on ACP740. DFWPE achieves 85.4% accuracy on ACP740 and 83.8% on the independent ACP240 test set, outperforming recent transformer-based predictors on overall metrics. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of both encoding branches and transfer learning. Interpretability analyses reveal length-dependent gating behavior consistent with biological structure, demonstrating that spectral-spatial decomposition provides robust and interpretable peptide representation for drug discovery.

title: DeepNPA: A protBert-based framework for residue-level annotation of neuropeptide precursors
abstract: Neuropeptides are key signaling molecules that regulate the nervous and endocrine systems, and their maturation depends on precise proteolytic cleavage of precursor proteins. However, residue-level annotation remains essential yet experimentally labor intensive, with limited dedicated computational tools. Here, we present DeepNPA, a residue-level annotation framework that integrates ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, with focal loss for imbalance-aware optimization. DeepNPA was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset annotated using the BIO scheme. On a held-out test dataset, DeepNPA achieved strong performance, with an accuracy of 0.953, an F1-score of 0.927, and an AUPRC of 0.965. On an independent benchmark dataset, DeepNPA outperformed NeuroCS and NeuroPred, achieving an ACC of 0.969 and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.666. External validation further demonstrated its ability to identify neuropeptide regions and their associated cleavage sites. In addition, we provided an online prediction platform to facilitate neuropeptide precursor annotation and cleavage site analysis.

title: Seeing the forest for the scenarios: Using decision trees to draw conclusions from large energy scenario sets
abstract: Energy transition studies often present hundreds of scenarios, yielding large datasets that are challenging to interpret. Alternative approaches define a few qualitative storylines, which are more accessible but disconnected from model-based evidence. Here, we show that decision trees, a popular machine learning technique, bridge this disconnect by distilling numerous scenarios into a small set of interpretable storylines centered around policy-relevant levers. We demonstrate this approach across three global and European case studies: First, we translate 1000 integrated assessment model scenarios into three storylines distinguished by their degrees of heating and industry electrification. Second, we show that 2°C warming pathways with continued fossil fuel usage only work under unusually mild climate responses. Third, we use 441 European pathways to show that high bioenergy or electrification are required for cost-effective climate neutrality. Our transferable approach helps decision-makers interpret large scenario sets by revealing how policy-relevant outputs are associated with different transition pathways.

title: An inverse-protein-folding pre-trained model for predicting the mutational effects in protein-protein interactions
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are fundamental to vast biological processes. Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in PPIs is crucial for protein engineering and drug discovery. Most existing PPI prediction approaches rely on refined physicochemical features or computationally intensive structural sampling. Here, we present delta-G message-passing-neural-network (DGMPNN), a message-passing neural-network framework for predicting the effects of mutations on PPIs. DGMPNN is pre-trained on an inverse protein folding (IPF) task and employs an adaptive residue-level attention pooling mechanism to enable effective transfer learning for predicting mutation-induced changes in protein binding affinity. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets and deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets. Experimental validation using computationally selected multi-site variants of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-hACE2 complex showed strong agreement between predicted and experimentally measured binding affinities.

title: Lactate as a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in cardiopulmonary bypass-associated acute kidney injury
abstract: Elevated lactate is a common metabolic perturbation following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). This study evaluates the clinical predictive value of lactate and explores its mechanism involving protein lactylation. Machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to multicenter intensive care databases identified preoperative lactate as a dominant predictor of CPB-acute kidney injury (AKI) risk. To validate these predictions biologically, rat CPB and cellular models were utilized. Experimental results demonstrated that CPB induces glycolytic reprogramming, lactate accumulation, and elevated pan-lysine lactylation. Inhibiting the production of lactate was associated with decreased protein lactylation, lower oxidative stress, and reduced local tissue inflammation, thereby mitigating renal injury. Collectively, our interpretable ML predictive models identify lactate as a top clinical predictor of CPB-AKI, while our experimental data establish the lactate-lactylation axis as a potential mechanistic pathway linking metabolic dysfunction to renal damage. This axis represents a candidate therapeutic target requiring further validation.

title: A source-target transfer learning framework with physics priors for subsurface chlorophyll reconstruction in the Northwest Pacific Ocean
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) distributions provide a foundation for understanding upper-ocean ecosystem dynamics and biogeochemical variability. We developed the source-target coupled network (ST-CoupleNet), a physics-guided transfer learning framework that combines Earth system model simulations with observation-constrained reconstructions to estimate subsurface Chl-a in the Northwest Pacific Ocean. The framework first learns large-scale spatiotemporal vertical representations from long-term CMIP6 simulations and then adapts them using reconstructed fields constrained by BioGeoChemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) observations, reducing simulation biases while preserving regional variability. By integrating dual-attention, residual learning, and convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) architectures, ST-CoupleNet substantially improves reconstruction accuracy over a conventional convolutional neural network (CNN). This framework demonstrates how transferable knowledge from climate simulations can be combined with autonomous observations to generate continuous 3D Chl-a fields, enabling large-scale investigations of subsurface marine ecosystems and biogeochemical change.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: Potential molecular links between triclosan exposure and osteoarthritis: An integrative systems toxicology study
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic disease affecting the entire joint, influenced by a combination of inflammatory, metabolic, immune, and environmental factors. Triclosan (TCS), a commonly used antimicrobial compound, has been linked to oxidative and immune disturbances; however, its molecular relevance to OA remains to be elucidated. This study integrated network toxicology, bulk transcriptomics, cross-cohort machine learning prioritization, immune infiltration analysis, single-cell transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and primary chondrocyte experiments. Thirty candidate genes related to both TCS and OA were identified, with CBR3, MAOA, MMP13, and AVPR1A being prioritized. Among these, CBR3 exhibited the most stable contribution to model predictions, widespread expression across OA chondrocyte subpopulations, and significant associations with inferred immune-cell composition. Supporting molecular docking and dynamics analyses indicated structural compatibility and dynamic feasibility between TCS and the four candidate proteins. In primary rat chondrocytes, low-dose TCS heightened reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, upregulated Cbr3 and Mmp13, downregulated Col2a1, Maoa, and Avpr1a, and increased CBR3 protein levels, with specific redox-related and matrix-related alterations becoming more pronounced under IL-1β stimulation. These findings contribute to a model that links TCS-associated redox disturbances to OA-relevant chondrocyte stress and matrix remodeling, providing candidate molecular connections for future mechanistic validation.

title: AI-driven environmental performance index using deep autoencoders for monitoring sustainable development goals
abstract: This study develops an autoencoder-based environmental performance index (AE_EPI) to assess environmental performance across 38 countries in five regions. Using a deep autoencoder, AE_EPI captures complex nonlinear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-region data and is benchmarked against a principal component analysis-based index (PCA_EPI). Linear Regression, Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost, combined with SHAP analysis, are used to identify key environmental drivers. Results show that AE_EPI outperforms PCA_EPI in reconstruction accuracy, stability, and robustness to noise, while RF yields the most consistent predictions. Globally, electricity access and renewable energy are the dominant drivers. Regionally, governance and innovation are most important in East Asia; urbanization in South Asia; renewable energy in Central Asia; digitalization in MENA; and economic capacity, electricity access, and governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. These findings support region-specific, data-driven policies that advance energy transitions, strengthen institutional capacity, and address local environmental priorities for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: PFOS exposure and periodontitis from adolescent burden to genetic and multiomics evidence
abstract: Periodontitis can develop early in life and may be influenced by persistent environmental exposures. We integrated Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, Mendelian randomization, transcriptomics, machine learning, immune profiling, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and in vitro validation to investigate links between perfluorooctane sulfonate exposure and periodontitis. Periodontal disease burden remained substantial among individuals aged 5–20 years and varied across sociodemographic strata. Genetically predicted PFOS exposure was associated with increased periodontitis risk by inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization. Multi-omics analyses identified 151 shared targets enriched in immune-inflammatory pathways and prioritized a ten-gene signature with strong diagnostic discrimination. Single-cell analysis implicated migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-centered immune communication, whereas molecular modeling supported stable PFOS-STK17B interactions. PFOS exposure in human gingival fibroblasts increased expression of the ten prioritized genes. These findings connect population burden with genetic, molecular, and experimental evidence supporting immune-inflammatory mechanisms linking PFOS exposure to periodontitis.

title: Breast cancer burden risk attribution and productivity loss in Chinese women aged 25 to 49
abstract: Breast cancer among Chinese women aged 25-49 years has substantial clinical and societal consequences. We integrated Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates for 1990-2023 with Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2022, United Nations population projections, International Labour Organization labour-force participation, and World Bank indicators. Incident cases rose from 50,064 to 87,221, while the weighted death rate declined from 9.25 to 4.72 per 100,000. Demographic changes explained 63.0% of additional cases. In exploratory extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) analyses interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), the fasting-plasma-glucose-related population attributable fraction (PAF) ranked first in several formulations but weakened after removing age and temporal structure; the selected high-body-mass-index (BMI) PAF series was constant at zero and unrankable. Potential mortality-related productivity loss was US$6.161 billion in 2023. Status-quo projections suggested increasing incidence through 2050 with very wide uncertainty, supporting surveillance and individual-level validation rather than immediate screening policy changes.

title: Antibiotic resistance genes in aquaculture: Molecular detection, environmental dynamics, and biological control strategies
abstract: Antibiotic resistance in aquaculture is a major threat to sustainable fish production and global public health. This review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of studies on antibiotic resistance in aquaculture published between 2005 and 2025, identified through a systematic and reproducible literature search. It clarifies the molecular basis of resistance, characterizes the environmental distribution of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and evaluates current and emerging control strategies in aquaculture systems. Evidence is organized into thematic domains encompassing molecular mechanisms, environmental reservoirs and drivers, diagnostic and surveillance tools, and biological alternatives to antibiotics. In parallel, vaccines, probiotics, and bacteriophage therapy show promising, context-dependent potential when embedded in multifaceted biocontrol frameworks. This review highlights priorities including protocol standardization, rapid farm-deployable diagnostics, and optimized synergistic biocontrol strategies, supported by artificial intelligence and big data analytics, to facilitate a transition from reactive treatment to preventive, system-level resistance management in aquaculture.

title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence
abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Here, we propose a hierarchical framework that reconceptualizes multisensory processing as a continuum of representational emergence across three distinct levels: level I (multimodal binding), where features are integrated via probabilistic causal inference; level II (supramodal representation), where recurrent co-activation and value-guided selection establish consolidated, perceptual-semantic engrams that act as emergent modalities; and level III (amodal concepts), where meaning becomes increasingly detached from sensory form and is represented within transmodal semantic networks. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Finally, we delineate an empirical roadmap and outline implications for supramodal AI, toward architectures capable of more autonomous semantic representation and generation.

title: A machine learning classifier reveals hidden rare biallelic heterozygous variants in the coding regions of Meniere disease genome
abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. We developed the MD classifier, an ML tool to distinguish familial from sporadic MD cases using rare variants in coding regions. We have generated a disease-specific gene variant score incorporating gene, variant, and disease-specific features. A gradient boosting classifier achieved the highest performance, with a test AUC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.702-0.948) and an accuracy of 81.5%. Reclassification of sporadic cases into the familial group ranged from 16.6% to 28.3%. The model identified a burden of biallelic heterozygous variants suggesting hidden recessive inheritance that may affect up to 38% of MD patients. Gene-enrichment analysis using major classifier features revealed distinct biological pathways between familial and sporadic MD. This ML-based framework integrates unique genetic features that may improve the diagnostic yield of rare disorders and is universally applicable to conditions with both familial and sporadic phenotypes, enabling the identification of compound heterozygous recessive inheritance.

title: Integrative genomics and experimental validation identify a mechanosensitive gene signature associated with colorectal cancer liver metastasis
abstract: The mechanical tumor microenvironment critically influences colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis, yet the underlying molecular mediators remain poorly defined. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics, bulk RNA-seq, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and 117 machine learning algorithms, we identified a six-gene mechanosensitive signature ( SNX7 , SDC1 , CDCP1 , PTGES , EMP2 , and CALB2 ) associated with CRC liver metastasis. This signature demonstrated superior prognostic performance (mean C-index 0.68) across multiple independent cohorts compared to 74 published CRC signatures. Among these genes, SDC1 was consistently upregulated in CRC cells and tissues, and its expression was further induced by increased matrix stiffness in tunable hydrogel culture systems. These findings support a mechanosensitive gene signature with robust prognostic value and identify SDC1 as a stiffness-responsive candidate regulator, providing insights into the mechanobiological regulation of CRC metastasis.

title: Deep learning based detection of active pulmonary tuberculosis from chest radiographs in a retrospective prospective multicenter study
abstract: Active tuberculosis remains a major global health problem, and distinguishing active from non-active disease on chest radiographs could accelerate triage where radiology resources are limited. We developed ShuffleNetV2 using 4,613 radiographs from two centers and evaluated it in retrospective external (1,318 patients) and prospective (560 patients) cohorts. The model achieved AUCs of 0.917 and 0.896, respectively, and performance was stable across prespecified demographic and scanner subgroups. In the prospective cohort, artificial-intelligence assistance increased radiologist AUCs to 0.897-0.937 across experience levels. These findings support ShuffleNetV2 as a rapid decision-support tool for prioritizing confirmatory clinical and microbiological assessment; positive predictions should not be used alone to initiate treatment.

title: Multivariate connectivity deviations reveal task-evoked and clinical network reorganization
abstract: Abstract Understanding how cognitive demands and pathology reshape large-scale functional connectivity (FC) requires methods that are both multivariate and region-specific. Here we introduce One-class SVM-based Connectome Anomaly Recognition (OSCAR), a normative modelling framework that detects condition-related deviations in the multivariate connectivity profile of a brain region. OSCAR learns the distribution of region-to-whole-brain connectivity patterns given a reference state sample (e.g. resting-state data; RS) using a one-class support vector machine (OCSVM). The trained models are then applied to FC profiles from a target condition (e.g., task or patient group). The outlier proportions are used to quantify the difference between the reference and target condition. We validated OSCAR on three diverse tasks and a patient cohort with early psychosis. OSCAR consistently identified condition-sensitive regions in networks known to support conflict processing, object-location memory, lexical learning, and early psychosis, respectively, including thalamic and basal ganglia regions. Moreover, it detected additional well-established task– or disease-relevant parcels not captured by the comparison method permutation-based multivariate analysis of variance (perMANOVA). Regions flagged by OSCAR were at least as close, and often closer, to independent task-activation findings than those identified by perMANOVA. These results demonstrate that OSCAR provides an interpretable, region-centred normative modelling approach that is sensitive to subtle multivariate FC deviations, and offers a practical tool for mapping condition-specific reconfigurations of functional brain networks with high external validity, in both experimental and clinical settings.

title: Artificial intelligence across the gastric cancer care continuum: Clinical evidence, multimodal integration, and translation
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across the gastric cancer care continuum, but its clinical maturity differs substantially among endoscopy, cross-sectional imaging, digital pathology, prognostic modeling, treatment selection, and surgical support. Existing reviews have often focused on individual modalities or summarized algorithmic performance without systematically distinguishing technical feasibility from translational readiness. We conducted a structured narrative review of studies indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE and the Web of Science Core Collection from January 2022 through July 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking. Earlier landmark studies were retained when necessary to explain the development of major applications. Priority was given to prospective, multicenter, externally validated, and clinically actionable studies. Evidence maturity was assessed according to study design, validation breadth, workflow relevance, calibration and clinical-utility assessment, and implementation evidence. The main constraint on gastric cancer AI is no longer pattern-recognition capability but the absence of reproducible clinical benefit under real-world conditions. Priorities include multiregional prospective validation, standardized calibration and decision curve assessment, comparison of clinicians with and without AI, integration into existing workflows, evaluation of economic and patient-level outcomes, and post-deployment monitoring.

title: Identification of mitophagy-related genes with diagnostic value in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis using bioinformatics analysis
abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a major cause of end-stage renal disease, involves podocyte injury and immune dysregulation. We integrated GEO transcriptomic datasets to identify 839 differentially expressed genes and 33 differential mitophagy-related genes via differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Machine learning identified six candidate diagnostic biomarkers, SLIRP, BLVRB, ATP6V1F, COX5B, TMEM14A, and TRMT112, with moderate-to-good discriminatory capacity across cohorts. xCell analysis revealed extensive renal immune remodeling in FSGS with expanded pro-inflammatory cells, diminished naive T cells and Tregs, and tight correlations between hub genes and immune profiles. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis suggested a trend of downregulation of hub genes in FSGS podocytes, alongside suppressed transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial energy metabolism and mitophagy-related pathways. qRT-PCR and western blot validated their downregulation at the whole-renal-tissue level in FSGS mouse models. These six genes may serve as diagnostic candidates and provide research clues for exploring mitophagy mechanisms in FSGS.

title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization
abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with static microenvironment analysis to identify enzyme variants compatible with biomimetic cofactors. Applied to P450BM3, a widely used biocatalyst for chiral synthesis and pharmaceutical precursor production, HelixWings identified a variant with a 404% improvement in catalytic efficiency toward cytochrome c under NMNH-supported conditions. The platform was further validated with CYP116B46, achieving a 217% improvement in NMNH utilization efficiency. HelixWings reduced screening time by 23-fold compared with rational design.

title: Recurrent latent dynamics in spinal circuits enable a digital twin of autonomic state transitions
abstract: Physiological signals underlying homeostasis, such as blood pressure, are dynamic and nonlinear, shaped by interactions among diverse neurons. During blood pressure transitions, neurons in the spinal intermediolateral nucleus (IML), a sympathetic hub, show heterogeneous monotonic increases or decreases in firing. Such diversity is intrinsic to homeostatic control but hampers accurate decoding of internal state dynamics. Here, we introduce a manifold-based model that addresses this challenge by directly mapping IML population activity onto physiological state transitions. Individual neurons responded independently with increases or decreases in firing, but these patterns alone did not align with the nonlinear trajectory of blood pressure. Focusing instead on recurrent population dynamics, we derived a low-dimensional circular manifold that captured the cyclical temporal evolution of state transitions. Embedding this manifold as a dynamic reservoir in a recurrent neural network reproduced both trial-by-trial variability in neural population activity and nonlinear blood pressure dynamics, establishing a circuit-level framework for autonomic state decoding.

title: ATP-free fatty aldehyde biosynthesis enables an autonomous lux-based bioluminescence system
abstract: Autonomous bioluminescence systems enable continuous light emission in engineered organisms by genetically encoding both luciferase enzymes and their substrate biosynthetic pathways, offering a powerful platform for non-invasive and long-term monitoring of biological processes. However, bioluminescence output is highly sensitive to substrate availability and host metabolic state, often leading to signal instability under energy-limited conditions. Here, we report an alternative luciferin biosynthetic strategy for the bacterial Lux bioluminescence system in which the adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent LuxEC complex is replaced by α-dioxygenase (αDOX), an enzyme that directly converts fatty acids into fatty aldehydes without consuming ATP. Using machine learning-guided directed evolution, we engineered αDOX variants that markedly enhanced bioluminescence intensity when coupled with bacterial luciferase. The resulting ATP-free Lux bioluminescence system enabled single-cell-level bioluminescence imaging and showed a smaller reduction in light emission than the native LuxCDABE system under several antibiotic treatments, although these experiments do not establish ATP availability as the causal mechanism.

title: Sexual dimorphisms of the olfactory system are conserved across bumblebee species
abstract: Bumblebees are integral to ecosystems as crucial pollinators. However, neuroscience has kept its focus on studying workers of commercially available species: Bombus terrestris (Europe), B . impatiens (North America), and B . ignitus (Asia). Here, we conducted a detailed comparative study of the brain and antennal anatomy in wild worker and male bumblebees of 6 common European species ( B. terrestris , B. pascuorum , B. pratorum , B. lapidarius , B. hypnorum , and B. lucorum ), with specific focus on their peripheral and central olfactory system. We found striking sexual dimorphisms that remain consistent across species and may underlie the differences in foraging preferences in bumblebees. We also developed a bespoke machine learning-based pipeline for automatic segmentation of confocal images of antennal lobes, which greatly speeds up the image analysis.

title: A physics-informed LLM agent for uncovering typhoon- and earthquake-induced turbine failures and offline yaw-pitch countermeasures
abstract: Extreme typhoons and earthquakes can cause severe damage to wind turbine structures, underscoring the need to better understand failure mechanisms and potential mitigation strategies. This study develops Iwind, a physics-informed large language model agent for wind-turbine engineering analysis. Supported by domain-specific training and multi-path retrieval-augmented generation, Iwind combines ReAct-style reasoning with the model context protocol to invoke the in-house physics solver Zwind for natural-language-driven load simulations. In the reported evaluations, Iwind outperformed its parent model on wind-turbine knowledge tasks and supported load-simulation execution and visual damage inspection. The collected cases showed blade fractures, tower buckling, and overturning under typhoon loading, while some earthquake-damaged turbines showed more pronounced damage in foundations or lower supporting structures. Parametric Zwind simulations further revealed W- and M-shaped offline yaw-pitch response manifolds for the investigated typhoon and earthquake cases, respectively, providing simulation-derived references for parked-state comparison and hazard-region identification. title: Neurocognition of dance: Guidelines for using dance as model behavior and research subject in cognitive neuroscience
abstract: Dance and movement science bridges cognitive psychology, neuroscience, cultural studies, philosophical aesthetics, and the performing arts. The field has evolved significantly, examining physical, social, psychological, and neural aspects of dance and movement execution and perception, contributing to a deeper understanding of human cognition and of dance itself. As the field expands, shared guidelines that support methodological rigor, reproducibility, and cultural relevance are of paramount importance. This paper synthesizes current research and introduces a comprehensive seven-principle research design framework for using dance in cognitive neuroscience. Key elements include the operationalization of "dance" in empirical sciences, the definition of who is a dancer, measures of expertise, and the importance of a culturally sensitive, holistic, and interdisciplinary approach to its investigation in the laboratory and in ecologically valid settings. This framework benefits research in dance and movement aesthetics, as well as investigations in social cognition, affective neuroscience, computer science, and artificial intelligence.

title: Tau spread plays an etiopathogenic connection between seizures and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) display heightened seizure susceptibility, in which neuronal hyperactivity during seizures correlates with exacerbated Tau pathology and cognitive impairment. This study integrated public transcriptomic datasets with machine learning approaches, suggesting Tau spread as a key biological association between seizure activity and AD. We validated activity-dependent Tau release under epileptic stimulation using primary neurons and human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC)-derived neuronal models. Further validation in an AAV-based mouse Tau propagation model revealed robust bidirectional interactions: pathological Tau overexpression worsened seizure outcomes, while seizures accelerated Tau propagation across brain regions, inducing neuronal loss and gliosis. This study characterizes the activity-regulated interplay between epileptic activity and AD-associated Tau pathology, offering a potential therapeutic target for AD comorbid with epilepsy.
